title: The Singhs Hold the Rear Guard as Abdali Closes In

blocks.text: Charat Singh accepts the elders' view that this is not the hour for ceremonial rearrangement but for sacrifice in defense of the Panth. The Singhs resolve to protect the moving caravan for the sake of their religion and ideology, even if that means exposing themselves as a rear guard.

They fight like lions against Biland Khan, Jahan Khan, and the pressing Pathan line, repeatedly throwing themselves into the path of the assault so women, children, and noncombatants can keep moving. Dust, noise, and repeated charges make the field chaotic, yet the Singhs continue to cover the retreat with their own bodies.

The crisis deepens when Ahmad Shah Abdali himself attacked the Singhs and pushes in from the rear with greater force. That intervention cuts off the Khalsa contingent from the moving Sikh caravan and turns the retreat into an even more desperate battle for survival.
